doc.title: Jim Hall — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Lenox, New York and Sonny Rollins
title: How travel and exploring cultures shaped his life
summary: Generalizations about nationalities don't hold up; he feels privileged to play around the world.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Well, one of the reasons I’m sort of asking about this is because as focused as he is and as you are on your music…
You also have lives outside of…
Or in addition to the music.
And so I thought that might be an interesting way to, to get into some other thoughts.
I’m sorry, I didn’t follow you.

To get, to ask you about other areas of interest. And I thought that there was a connection there. Maybe there isn’t but… the connection of, of what you as a musician and a traveler and an explorer of cultures…
…people, what… you know, how that shaped your life and your music.

Yeah. Well, you do… one does. One do… (laughs) see things differently. And people who make generalizations about nationalities and color and stuff, you say, well, that’s, you know… (laughs) I was there, dummy, and they ain’t like that at all, you know, so… Yeah, so… And, and yeah, generalizations are, in general, can get you in terrible trouble, I think, and… Yeah, I feel very privileged to have first of all made a, made a living so far, doing something that I really care about. And I get paid to go to these fantastic places. You usually get paid and meet amazing people and… I like to say that I’ve played music with people with whom I couldn’t have a conversation. Of course, some of them were New Yorkers but… (laughs) That’s, that’s great, though, you know, I just played with, you know, people in Japan and Europe and all over.
